items.requirement: A requested deployment fails when no Kubernetes manifest is supplied.
The fixture consumes one explicit checked-manifest artifact.
The fixture verifies the manifest media type, size, digest, and local artifact URL.
The deployment selects one service name and one service port.
The deployed workload uses the requested application image.
The fixture accepts only an immutable image digest from an allowed local registry.
The declared digest must match the digest in the image reference.
The fixture does not build or promote an image during deployment.
The runtime accepts multi-document Kubernetes YAML.
The runtime applies the exact checked bytes without image or namespace rewriting.
The runtime rejects explicit manifest namespaces before deployment.
The runtime rejects cluster-scoped Kubernetes resources.
Every workload image must use an immutable SHA-256 digest.
At least one workload must use the selected application image.
Resource count and manifest bytes have operator limits.
The runtime requests an isolated namespace through BusterNamespaceLease.
The runtime verifies create, get, and delete lease permissions.
The runtime performs a server-side dry-run before creating the lease.
The runtime uses a deterministic attempt-scoped lease and namespace name.
The runtime waits for the namespace controller to report Ready.
A rejected, failed, or timed-out lease cannot produce a fixture output.
The runtime applies the declared resources in the leased namespace.
The runtime waits until at least one workload pod exists.
Every observed workload pod must report Ready.
A readiness timeout is an execution failure.
The fixture returns one typed deployment value.
The result includes the namespace and internal service endpoint.
The result includes creation time, expiry time, and release action.
The result binds the applied manifest digest and immutable image reference.
The lease can copy declared test-deployment Secrets.
The fixture returns Secret references without reading Secret values.
The fixture does not place decoded Secret values in logs or outputs.
The default cleanup mode deletes the namespace lease after dependent work.
Cleanup is a mandatory fixture lifecycle operation.
Cleanup can recover from a provider-process restart with deterministic identity.
A retained fixture has a bounded controller-enforced expiry.
A human can release a retained fixture with the returned action.
The fixture prepares resources and does not make a product quality decision.
The fixture does not expose the service publicly.
The fixture does not run an HTTP content test.
The fixture does not run Helm, Kustomize, or manifest lint.
The provider receives only the narrow kubernetes.fixture capability.
Manifest paths must remain inside the run-owned root.
The capability restricts namespace prefixes and registry repositories.
Cancellation or timeout cannot produce a passing fixture result.
The provider is not retry-safe and defaults to zero retries.
The replacement cannot control the gate during implementation or parity.
The old k8s suite remains the sole authority until cutover.
